title: Eight Weeks Out of Hiding
subtitle: An eight week plan from James Bell for the one who can't stop looking at porn. Telling one person, your hardest hour, honest accountability, the body as a gift, and grace for the day you fall.
intro:
This is an eight week plan for the one who keeps going back to porn and can't stop, whether you're a man or a woman, single or married, or a teenager who has carried this alone. Each week holds one focus, one small daily practice, one thing to read, one tool to use, and one honest question. It walks the ground of the care page on pornography more slowly, from telling one person, through your hardest hour and the hunger underneath it, to accountability that isn't surveillance, the people it touches, the goodness of the body, grace on the day you fall, and a life where you're known. Shame drives this cycle, so you won't find condemnation here. You won't find easy reassurance either, because both leave you alone with it.

It isn't a cure, and it isn't a substitute for a doctor, a licensed counselor, a pastor, or real people who know your name. If you've tried to stop and can't, a counselor trained in compulsive sexual behavior is worth the call. If the shame has turned into thoughts of ending your life, call or text 988 tonight, before anything else here. You may fall during these weeks; week seven is written for that morning, so turn to it whenever you need it. Walk the plan imperfectly. A missed week is not failure; you just pick it back up. Your check marks are saved only in this browser.
careNote: If you've tried to stop and can't, or it's costing you sleep, work, money, or your marriage, see a licensed counselor trained in compulsive sexual behavior, and if someone hurt you sexually, now or long ago, the Find Help page lists RAINN's hotline. In a crisis, call or text 988.

weeks.why: You've told yourself it was the last time, maybe more times than you can count, and the shame afterward has kept you quiet. But the quiet is where this grows. A psalm that bears David's name describes what hiding does to a person: "When I kept silent, my bones became brittle from my groaning all day long" (Psalm 32:3). You've tried beating this alone and in secret, and it hasn't held. The letter of James sets confession beside healing: "confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed" (James 5:16). So the first step is telling one person the truth, someone mature who will keep your confidence and won't flinch or shrug it off.
weeks.practice: Choose your person: a pastor, a counselor, an older friend of your own sex, or, if you're a teenager, a parent or another adult you trust. Each day, pray for them by name. Before the week ends, tell them in plain words that you've been struggling with pornography and can't stop on your own. If you're married, your spouse deserves the truth too; week five is about telling them well, and you can read it now.

read.label: Pornography and Its Grip, a short page on why the way out begins with bringing the secret into the light

tool.label: The Prayer Generator's prayers before a hard conversation, for the hour before you tell someone

weeks.reflection: Who is one person I could tell the whole truth to this week, and what am I afraid will happen if I do?

weeks.why: It rarely comes out of nowhere. Usually it keeps a schedule: the same hour, the same room, the same screen, often late at night or at the end of a hard day. David's fall began on an evening when the army had gone to war and the king had stayed home. He got up from his bed, walked on the palace roof, and from there he saw Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11:1-3). Paul's counsel is to "make no provision for the desires of the flesh" (Romans 13:14). Jesus said to cut off the hand that causes you to sin (Matthew 5:30). He wasn't asking anyone to harm their body; he meant cut off whatever feeds it. Today that usually means changing the setup as well as your resolve. Don't prop the door open and then pray you won't walk through it.
weeks.practice: Each night this week, charge your phone outside the room where you sleep. Write down when, where, and how you felt the last few times it happened, and look for your hour. Change one thing about that hour: a set bedtime, a different room, other people around. Turn on the content restrictions built into your devices, let someone else hold the passcode, and delete the apps, accounts, and searches that lead you there.

read.label: Temptation, on fighting it upstream by removing what feeds it and planning your escape in advance

tool.label: The Verse Finder's Temptation verses, 1 Corinthians 10:13 among them, to carry into your weakest hour

weeks.reflection: When, where, and on what screen does this usually happen, and what have I left open that I could close this week?

weeks.focus: What the urge is really asking for
weeks.why: Look at what you wrote down last week and notice what came just before: lonely, bored, stressed, angry, rejected, exhausted. Porn offers relief without risk, closeness with no one who could turn you away, being wanted without being known. It's a counterfeit of something good, and the hunger underneath it is real. In the book of Isaiah, God asks, "Why spend money on that which is not bread, and your labor on that which does not satisfy?" (Isaiah 55:2). Naming the need doesn't excuse the habit, and loneliness doesn't make it right. But you'll keep reaching for bread that can't feed you until you know what you're actually hungry for, and bring that hunger to God and to people who can meet it.
weeks.practice: Each day, when the urge comes, stop and name in a word or two what you're feeling. Then give that need something real. If you're lonely, call or text someone. If you're bored, get up and do something with your hands. If you're stressed or worn out, pray one honest sentence and rest, or go to bed if it's late. Write the feeling down each time, so by the week's end you can see the pattern.

read.label: How Do You Fight Temptation and Disordered Desire? On the hunger underneath the want

tool.label: The Emotional Health Self-Check, which begins with naming what you feel in the moment, a mirror and not a diagnosis

weeks.reflection: What was I really hungry for the last time I gave in, and where could I have taken that hunger instead?

weeks.why: A filter can block a site, and a report can show someone where your phone has been. Both can help with the setup, but neither can make you honest, and relied on alone they can turn into a show, a clean report standing in for a clean heart while the real fight moves to another device. Accountability is a person who knows the truth and asks real questions. The letter to the Hebrews tells believers to "exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin's deceitfulness" (Hebrews 3:13). Sin deceives the one it holds, so you need someone outside your own head, and that person can only help if you tell the truth before you're asked. If you're married, don't make your spouse your monitor. They were the one wronged, and they need care of their own.
weeks.practice: Ask the person you told in week one, or another mature believer of your own sex, to talk with you at a set time each week. If you're a teenager, make it a parent or an adult your parents know about. Give them three questions to ask every time: when it last happened, what was going on before it, and what you haven't told them. Answer before they ask, and text them the same day you fall or come close.

read.label: Why Christians Confess Their Sins Out Loud, on why a secret loses its hold once it's told to someone who stays

tool.label: Friendship: A Bible Study on the Love We Forgot, whose third session is on the faithful wounds of a friend

weeks.reflection: Is there anything I'm still keeping from the person who holds me accountable, and what am I protecting by keeping it?

weeks.why: Porn tells you it's private and nobody gets hurt. It isn't true. The people on the screen are real, made in the image of God (Genesis 1:27), somebody's son or daughter, and you can't know what was done to put them there. If you're married, it's also a betrayal. Jesus spoke of lust as adultery in the heart (Matthew 5:28), so don't soften it, and don't treat your spouse's hurt as an overreaction. They deserve the whole truth, told at once, though not on impulse and not alone. Let them set the pace of whatever comes next. They need care of their own, and the care page has a part written for them. If anything you've seen shows someone under eighteen, that's a crime: report it to the police, or if you're a teenager, tell a parent or another adult you trust, who can report it.
weeks.practice: Each day, practice seeing one person you meet as a person and not a body: look them in the eye, use their name, and pray for them that night. If you're married and your spouse doesn't know, ask your pastor or counselor this week to help you plan how to tell them. If they already know, don't ask them to watch you or carry your guilt, and let them know the care page has a part for them.

read.label: Lust and the Wandering Eye, on how lust turns someone made in God's image into a thing to be used

tool.label: I can't stop looking at porn, the care page, with a part written for the spouse who found out

weeks.reflection: Who has been hurt by what I've hidden, including people I'll never meet, and have I let myself see them as people?

weeks.focus: The body God made and bought
weeks.why: For a generation, many churches taught purity mostly as rules and warnings, as if the body itself were the problem, and as a pastor I don't stand outside that failure. Scripture starts somewhere else. God made us male and female (Genesis 1:27) and looked at all he had made, "and indeed, it was very good" (Genesis 1:31). Desire is a gift. Lust is desire cut loose from the person, wanting to take instead of to give. When some in the church at Corinth used slogans that treated the body as unimportant, Paul answered, "The body is not intended for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body" (1 Corinthians 6:13). Shame treats your body as something to despise. Paul says you were "bought at a price" (1 Corinthians 6:20), body included, and God means to raise it (1 Corinthians 6:14).
weeks.practice: Each day, thank God for one thing your body does well: it carries you, works, rests, heals. When the pull comes, don't panic or despise yourself. Tell God honestly that you want this and you want to want him more, then turn your attention to something real. Once this week, read 1 Corinthians 6:12-20 slowly, out loud if you can.

read.label: How to Honor Your Body as a Christian, on a body God made good, bought, and means to raise

tool.label: 1 Corinthians 6 in the Study Bible, where Paul answers slogans that treated the body as unimportant

weeks.reflection: Have I treated my body and my desires as enemies, and what would change if I believed God made them good and paid for them?

weeks.focus: Grace on the day you fall
weeks.why: You may fall during these weeks, and shame will say you've already blown it, so you might as well keep going. Refuse it. Self-disgust feels like holiness, but it sends you back into hiding. Paul wrote to the Corinthians: "Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death" (2 Corinthians 7:10). Psalm 51 bears David's name, and its heading sets it after Nathan confronted him. It asks for what none of us can make on our own: "Create in me a clean heart, O God" (Psalm 51:10). The first letter of John was written "so that you will not sin," and its next words are "But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father" (1 John 2:1). You fight from forgiveness, not for it. If the shame turns into thoughts of ending your life, call or text 988 now.
weeks.practice: Each night, tell God what happened that day, the good and the bad, and pray Psalm 51:10-12 as your own. If you fall, don't wait for a better week. Tell God that night and your person the next day, write down what led up to it, and change one thing. The book of Micah gives words for that morning: "Though I have fallen, I will arise" (Micah 7:8).

read.label: How to Confess Sin and Walk in Repentance, on naming the sin, receiving forgiveness as done, and turning

tool.label: Psalm 51 in the Study Bible, the prayer for a clean heart that bears David's name, with notes on its setting

weeks.reflection: When I fall, do I run toward God or away from him, and what does that tell me about who I think he is?

weeks.why: Porn offered a way to look without being seen. You were made for the reverse. Before the hiding, "the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed" (Genesis 2:25), fully seen and fully safe. The gospel offers something harder and better: to be seen completely, and kept. Jesus called his disciples friends on the night they would desert him (John 15:15). The first letter of John says, "if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another" (1 John 1:7). Build a life with friends who know the truth and a table you share. If you're married, closeness can only come back at the pace of rebuilt trust, and your spouse sets that pace; pressing for it is a harm of its own. These weeks may not end the fight. They were meant to end the hiding.
weeks.practice: Write on a card the two or three practices from these weeks that helped most, with when and where you'll keep them, and show it to your person. Each day, take one step toward real friendship: a call, a shared meal, an honest answer when someone asks how you are. Keep your weekly talk going after the plan ends.

read.label: Why Is It So Hard to Make Real Friends as an Adult? On covenant friendship and going first with the truth

tool.label: The Rule of Life Builder, to keep what helped, with choices like one friend who knows the truth about you and a guardrail on screens

weeks.reflection: Who knows the truth about me now, and what will I do to keep it that way when these eight weeks are over?
